question:
switch (x) { case 1: case 2: printf("1 or 2"); break; default: printf("other"); }
For x=1, what is printed?
options: 1 or 2 (case 1 falls through to case 2, break exits)
other (default is always executed)
Compiler error: empty case
Nothing (no matching case)
explanation: Empty case labels fall through; case 1 falls to case 2 which has the code; break exits the switch.

options: false (assignment x = 0 executes, returns 0, which is false in the if condition)
true (5 is truthy)
Compiler error: assignment in if condition
Both true and false (both branches execute)
explanation: The assignment x = 0 evaluates to 0, which is falsy; the else branch executes.

options: 0 2 (i=1 skips the printf due to continue)
0 1 2 (continue jumps to the next iteration, still printing i=1)
0 (continue exits the loop)
Compiler error: continue outside loop
explanation: continue skips the rest of the loop body and jumps to the next iteration; when i=1, printf is skipped.

options: To loop until a random condition is met; risky because the condition might never occur or take very long
To guarantee the loop exits after exactly one iteration
break is required syntax; loops cannot exit otherwise
To ensure the loop never exits (infinite loop by design)
explanation: while(1) is an intentional infinite loop; break provides the exit condition, but relying on random chance is unreliable.

options: Once (do-while executes at least once; break prevents looping)
Zero times (while(0) prevents the loop)
Twice (do-while always loops at least twice)
Compiler error: break in do-while
explanation: do-while executes the body once before checking the condition; break exits, and while(0) never loops.

options: Nothing (outer if fails; else binds to inner if, not outer)
B (else always executes)
A (y > 10 is true)
Compiler error: ambiguous if-else
explanation: else binds to the nearest if; when x ≤ 5, the outer if body (including the inner if-else) is skipped entirely.

skipped reached (goto executes the next statement, then continues)
Compiler error: goto is not allowed
skipped (goto is a no-op)
explanation: goto transfers control to the label, skipping all code in between; it is rarely used but valid for error unwinding.

options: To break out of nested loops (break only exits one level; goto exits to the label)
To optimize the loop performance
To ensure the loop always prints exactly once
goto is not necessary; break handles nested loops
explanation: break only exits the innermost loop; goto can break out of multiple nested levels in one jump.
